passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: 1. A sacrament is a visible sign of invisible grace, instituted by Jesus Christ for our sanctification.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: St. Thomas defines a sacrament as an outward, sensible sign instituted by Jesus Christ that imparts invisible sanctifying grace to the soul.
passages.fullText: 1. A sacrament is a visible sign of invisible grace, instituted by Jesus Christ for our sanctification.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: 2. Just as the natural life of man requires birth, growth, nourishment, healing from disease, recovery of strength, social governance, and propagation, so the supernatural life of grace requires the seven Sacraments. 3. The seven Sacraments of the New Law are: Baptism, Confirmation, the Holy Eucharist, Penance, Extreme Unction, Holy Orders, and Matrimony.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: By analogy to the physical and social necessities of natural human life, the supernatural life of grace requires the seven Sacraments of the New Law.
passages.fullText: 2. Just as the natural life of man requires birth, growth, nourishment, healing from disease, recovery of strength, social governance, and propagation, so the supernatural life of grace requires the seven Sacraments. 3. The seven Sacraments of the New Law are: Baptism, Confirmation, the Holy Eucharist, Penance, Extreme Unction, Holy Orders, and Matrimony.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: 4. Each sacrament consists of sensible matter (actions or elements) and sacred form (the words spoken by the minister), conferring grace through the power of Christ's Passion.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Every sacrament is composed of sensible matter and sacramental form, deriving its efficacy to confer sanctifying grace from the merits of the Passion of Christ.
passages.fullText: 4. Each sacrament consists of sensible matter (actions or elements) and sacred form (the words spoken by the minister), conferring grace through the power of Christ's Passion.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Baptism is the sacrament of spiritual regeneration through water and the Word of God, as Christ commanded in Matthew 28:19: "Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Baptism is the sacrament of spiritual rebirth instituted by Christ through water and the invocation of the Most Holy Trinity.
passages.fullText: 1. Baptism is the sacrament of spiritual regeneration through water and the Word of God, as Christ commanded in Matthew 28:19: "Baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: It cleanses the soul from original sin and all actual sins, remits all eternal and temporal punishment due to sin, and imprints an indelible spiritual character marking the recipient as a member of Christ.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Baptism entirely cancels the guilt and punishment of original and actual sin while imprinting an indelible character configuring the recipient to Christ.
passages.fullText: 2. It cleanses the soul from original sin and all actual sins, remits all eternal and temporal punishment due to sin, and imprints an indelible spiritual character marking the recipient as a member of Christ.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: It infuses sanctifying grace, the theological virtues of faith, hope, and charity, and makes the baptized an adopted child of God and heir to the kingdom of heaven (John 3:5).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Through Baptism, the soul is infused with sanctifying grace and the theological virtues, becoming an adopted child of God and heir to heaven.
passages.fullText: 3. It infuses sanctifying grace, the theological virtues of faith, hope, and charity, and makes the baptized an adopted child of God and heir to the kingdom of heaven (John 3:5).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The ordinary minister of Baptism is a bishop, priest, or deacon, but in case of necessity any person using true water and the Trinitarian form can validly baptize.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: While ordained clergy serve as ordinary ministers of Baptism, in cases of necessity anyone can validly administer the sacrament using water and the Trinitarian form.
passages.fullText: 4. The ordinary minister of Baptism is a bishop, priest, or deacon, but in case of necessity any person using true water and the Trinitarian form can validly baptize.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Confirmation is the sacrament that strengthens and matures the spiritual life begun in Baptism, making the recipient a strong and perfect Christian and soldier of Jesus Christ.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Confirmation perfects baptismal grace by maturing the spiritual life and equipping the believer as a strong soldier of Jesus Christ.
passages.fullText: 1. Confirmation is the sacrament that strengthens and matures the spiritual life begun in Baptism, making the recipient a strong and perfect Christian and soldier of Jesus Christ.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The matter of this sacrament is the anointing with holy chrism (consecrated olive oil and balsam) on the forehead accompanied by the imposition of hands by the Bishop (Acts 8:14-17).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The sacramental matter of Confirmation consists of the imposition of hands and anointing with consecrated chrism administered by a bishop.
passages.fullText: 2. The matter of this sacrament is the anointing with holy chrism (consecrated olive oil and balsam) on the forehead accompanied by the imposition of hands by the Bishop (Acts 8:14-17).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The form consists of the words: "I sign thee with the sign of the Cross, and I confirm thee with the chrism of salvation, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The essential form of Confirmation confers spiritual sealing through the sign of the Cross and the invocation of the Holy Trinity.
passages.fullText: 3. The form consists of the words: "I sign thee with the sign of the Cross, and I confirm thee with the chrism of salvation, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: It imprints an indelible character and imparts the sevenfold gifts of the Holy Ghost: Wisdom, Understanding, Counsel, Fortitude, Knowledge, Piety, and Fear of the Lord (Isaiah 11:2).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Confirmation permanently seals the soul with an indelible character and imparts the sevenfold gifts of the Holy Spirit.
passages.fullText: 4. It imprints an indelible character and imparts the sevenfold gifts of the Holy Ghost: Wisdom, Understanding, Counsel, Fortitude, Knowledge, Piety, and Fear of the Lord (Isaiah 11:2).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: 1. The Holy Eucharist is the greatest of all sacraments, containing really, truly, and substantially the Body, Blood, Soul, and Divinity of our Lord Jesus Christ under the appearances of bread and wine.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Holy Eucharist is the preeminent sacrament because it substantially contains the Body, Blood, Soul, and Divinity of Jesus Christ under the sacramental species.
passages.fullText: 1. The Holy Eucharist is the greatest of all sacraments, containing really, truly, and substantially the Body, Blood, Soul, and Divinity of our Lord Jesus Christ under the appearances of bread and wine.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: 2. At the Last Supper, Christ instituted this sublime sacrament and sacrifice when He took bread, blessed, broke, and gave it to His disciples, saying: "This is My Body," and over the chalice: "This is My Blood of the new testament, which shall be shed for many unto remission of sins" (Matthew 26:26-28).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christ instituted the Eucharist at the Last Supper as the sacrament and sacrifice of the New Covenant for the remission of sins.
passages.fullText: 2. At the Last Supper, Christ instituted this sublime sacrament and sacrifice when He took bread, blessed, broke, and gave it to His disciples, saying: "This is My Body," and over the chalice: "This is My Blood of the new testament, which shall be shed for many unto remission of sins" (Matthew 26:26-28).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: 3. By the words of consecration spoken by the priest, the whole substance of the bread is converted into the Body of Christ, and the whole substance of the wine into His Blood, which marvelous change the Church terms Transubstantiation.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Through the priest's pronunciation of the words of consecration, the entire substance of bread and wine is converted into the Body and Blood of Christ by Transubstantiation.
passages.fullText: 3. By the words of consecration spoken by the priest, the whole substance of the bread is converted into the Body of Christ, and the whole substance of the wine into His Blood, which marvelous change the Church terms Transubstantiation.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: 4. The Eucharist is both a sacrament that nourishes the soul with divine life and the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass that perpetuates Calvary upon our altars (John 6:54).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Holy Eucharist simultaneously serves to nourish the soul with divine life as a sacrament and to perpetuate the sacrifice of the Cross upon the altar.
passages.fullText: 4. The Eucharist is both a sacrament that nourishes the soul with divine life and the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass that perpetuates Calvary upon our altars (John 6:54).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Penance is the sacrament instituted by Christ for the forgiveness of sins committed after Baptism (John 20:23).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Sacrament of Penance was instituted by Christ for the remission of sins committed after Baptism.
passages.fullText: 1. Penance is the sacrament instituted by Christ for the forgiveness of sins committed after Baptism (John 20:23).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The essential acts of the penitent are three: Contrition (heartfelt sorrow for sin with purpose of amendment), Confession (sincere accusation of all mortal sins to an authorized priest), and Satisfaction (performance of the penance enjoined by the confessor).
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The three essential acts required of the penitent in the Sacrament of Penance are contrition, confession to an authorized priest, and satisfaction.
passages.fullText: 2. The essential acts of the penitent are three: Contrition (heartfelt sorrow for sin with purpose of amendment), Confession (sincere accusation of all mortal sins to an authorized priest), and Satisfaction (performance of the penance enjoined by the confessor).

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: The form of the sacrament is the judicial absolution pronounced by the priest: "I absolve thee from thy sins in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The sacramental form of Penance consists in the judicial words of absolution pronounced by the priest in the name of the Holy Trinity.
passages.fullText: 3. The form of the sacrament is the judicial absolution pronounced by the priest: "I absolve thee from thy sins in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: This sacrament restores sanctifying grace, reconciles the sinner with God and the Church, and revives merits lost through sin.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Sacrament of Penance restores sanctifying grace, reconciles the soul to God and the Church, and revives merits forfeited by sin.
passages.fullText: 4. This sacrament restores sanctifying grace, reconciles the sinner with God and the Church, and revives merits lost through sin.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Extreme Unction (the Anointing of the Sick) is the sacrament instituted by Christ to confer spiritual comfort, strength, and bodily relief to the faithful who are in danger of death through sickness or old age.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Extreme Unction, grounded in Apostolic teaching from St. James, confers spiritual fortitude, remission of sins, defense against final demonic assaults, and bodily relief for the dying.
passages.fullText:
1. Extreme Unction (the Anointing of the Sick) is the sacrament instituted by Christ to confer spiritual comfort, strength, and bodily relief to the faithful who are in danger of death through sickness or old age.

2. The Apostle James describes this sacrament in James 5:14-15: "Is any man sick among you? Let him bring in the priests of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord. And the prayer of faith shall save the sick man: and the Lord shall raise him up: and if he be in sins, they shall be forgiven him."

3. It remits venial sins, cleanses remaining temporal punishment, strengthens the soul against final demonic assaults, and restores bodily health if expedient for the soul's salvation.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Holy Orders is the sacrament by which spiritual power and grace are conferred upon bishops, priests, and deacons to exercise sacred liturgical ministries and shepherd the flock of Christ.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Sacrament of Holy Orders confers spiritual power, grace, and an indelible character through the imposition of hands and consecratory prayer, enabling ministers to shepherd the flock, consecrate the Eucharist, and forgive sins.
passages.fullText:
1. Holy Orders is the sacrament by which spiritual power and grace are conferred upon bishops, priests, and deacons to exercise sacred liturgical ministries and shepherd the flock of Christ.

2. The essential rite consists of the imposition of hands by the consecrating bishop and the solemn consecratory prayer (2 Timothy 1:6).

3. It imprints an indelible spiritual character upon the soul of the minister, configuring him to Christ the eternal High Priest and granting power to consecrate the Holy Eucharist and forgive sins.

passages.author: St. Thomas Aquinas (Trans. Joseph B. Collins)
passages.keyExcerpt: Matrimony is the sacrament instituted by God in Paradise and elevated by Christ to sacramental dignity, uniting a Christian man and woman in an indissoluble bond of marital fidelity (Genesis 2:24; Matthew 19:6). It signifies the mystical union between Christ and His holy Church.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Holy Matrimony is an indissoluble sacrament signifying the union of Christ and the Church, imparting sacramental grace to spouses for mutual sanctification and the Christian raising of children.
passages.fullText: 1. Matrimony is the sacrament instituted by God in Paradise and elevated by Christ to sacramental dignity, uniting a Christian man and woman in an indissoluble bond of marital fidelity (Genesis 2:24; Matthew 19:6). 2. It signifies the mystical union between Christ and His holy Church, as the Apostle Paul teaches in Ephesians 5:32: "This is a great sacrament; but I speak in Christ and in the Church." 3. It confers special grace upon the spouses to live in mutual love, assist each other in holiness, and raise children in the fear and love of God.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 1. There are two ways, one of life and one of death, and there is a great difference between the two ways. 2. The way of life is this. 3. First of all, thou shalt love the God that made thee; 4. secondly, thy neighbour as thyself.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Way of Life is founded upon the supreme commandments to love God the Creator and love one's neighbor as oneself, observing the Golden Rule.
passages.fullText: 1. There are two ways, one of life and one of death, and there is a great difference between the two ways. 2. The way of life is this. 3. First of all, thou shalt love the God that made thee; 4. secondly, thy neighbour as thyself. 5. And all things whatsoever thou wouldest not have befal thyself neither do thou unto another.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 7. Bless them that curse you, and pray for your enemies and fast for them that persecute you; 8. for what thank is it, if ye love them that love you? Do not even the Gentiles the same? But do ye love them that hate you, and ye shall not have an enemy.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christian charity transcends natural affection by requiring believers to bless, pray, fast, and extend supernatural love toward their enemies and persecutors.
passages.fullText: 6. Now of these words the doctrine is this. 7. Bless them that curse you, and pray for your enemies and fast for them that persecute you; 8. for what thank is it, if ye love them that love you? Do not even the Gentiles the same? But do ye love them that hate you, and ye shall not have an enemy.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 9. Abstain thou from fleshly and bodily lusts. 10. If any man give thee a blow on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also, and thou shalt be perfect;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christian perfection demands bodily self-restraint, patient endurance of injuries, radical meekness, and detachment from worldly possessions.
passages.fullText: 9. Abstain thou from fleshly and bodily lusts. 10. If any man give thee a blow on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also, and thou shalt be perfect; 11. if a man impress thee to go with him, one mile, go with him twain; 12. if a man take away thy cloak, give him thy coat also; 13. if a man take away from thee that which is thine own, ask it not back, for neither art thou able.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 14. To every man that asketh of thee give, and ask not back; 15. for the Father desireth that gifts be given to all from His own bounties. 16. Blessed is he that giveth according to the commandment; 17. for he is guiltless.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Almsgiving reflects the Father's universal bounty and brings blessings to the cheerful giver, while taking charity without genuine need incurs moral accountability.
passages.fullText: 14. To every man that asketh of thee give, and ask not back; 15. for the Father desireth that gifts be given to all from His own bounties. 16. Blessed is he that giveth according to the commandment; 17. for he is guiltless. 18. Woe to him that receiveth; 19. for, if a man receiveth having need, he is guiltless; 20. but he that hath no need shall give satisfaction why and wherefore he received;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 21. and being put in confinement he shall be examined concerning the deeds that he hath done, and he shall not come out thence until he hath given back the last farthing.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Those who take alms fraudulently or without need will undergo strict examination and remain in confinement until full restitution is made.
passages.fullText: 21. and being put in confinement he shall be examined concerning the deeds that he hath done, and he shall not come out thence until he hath given back the last farthing.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 23. Let thine alms sweat into thine hands, until thou shalt have learnt to whom to give.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Prudence and discernment must guide charitable giving so that alms are distributed purposefully to those genuinely in need.
passages.fullText: 22. Yea, as touching this also it is said; 23. Let thine alms sweat into thine hands, until thou shalt have learnt to whom to give.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: We give Thee thanks, Holy Father, for Thy holy name, which Thou hast made to tabernacle in our hearts, and for the knowledge and faith and immortality, which Thou hast made known unto us through Thy Son Jesus; Thine is the glory for ever and ever.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Following Communion, the faithful give thanks to the Father for His indwelling presence, divine knowledge, faith, and immortality revealed through Jesus Christ.
passages.fullText: 1. And after ye are satisfied thus give ye thanks: 2. We give Thee thanks, Holy Father, for Thy holy name, which Thou hast made to tabernacle in our hearts, and for the knowledge and faith and immortality, which Thou hast made known unto us through Thy Son Jesus; 3. Thine is the glory for ever and ever.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou, Almighty Master, didst create all things for Thy name's sake, and didst give food and drink unto men for enjoyment, that they might render thanks to Thee; but didst bestow upon us spiritual food and drink and eternal life through Thy Son.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: God the Creator grants material sustenance to humanity for enjoyment, but bestows upon the faithful the superior gift of spiritual food, drink, and eternal life in Christ.
passages.fullText: 4. Thou, Almighty Master, didst create all things for Thy name's sake, and didst give food and drink unto men for enjoyment, that they might render thanks to Thee; 5. but didst bestow upon us spiritual food and drink and eternal life through Thy Son. 6. Before all things we give Thee thanks that Thou art powerful; 7. Thine is the glory for ever and ever.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Remember, Lord, Thy Church to deliver it from all evil and to perfect it in Thy love; and gather it together from the four winds—even the Church which has been sanctified—into Thy kingdom which Thou hast prepared for it;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The post-Communion prayer implores God to protect, sanctify, and unite His Church in charity, gathering her from all nations into the prepared heavenly kingdom.
passages.fullText: 8. Remember, Lord, Thy Church to deliver it from all evil and to perfect it in Thy love; 9. and gather it together from the four winds—even the Church which has been sanctified—into Thy kingdom which Thou hast prepared for it; 10. for Thine is the power and the glory for ever and ever.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: If any man is holy, let him come; if any man is not, let him repent. Maran Atha. Amen.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The early liturgical acclamation invites those in a state of holiness to approach the sacred mysteries while admonishing sinners to repent before the Lord's coming.
passages.fullText: 11. May grace come and may this world pass away. 12. Hosanna to the God of David. 13. If any man is holy, let him come; 14. if any man is not, let him repent. Maran Atha. Amen.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But permit the prophets to offer thanksgiving as much as they desire.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache establishes a liturgical rubric granting recognized prophets the freedom to offer spontaneous Eucharistic thanksgiving in communal assembly.
passages.fullText: 15. But permit the prophets to offer thanksgiving as much as they desire.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 1. Whosoever therefore shall come and teach you all these things that have been said before, receive him; 2. but if the teacher himself be perverted and teach a different doctrine to the destruction thereof, hear him not; 3. but if to the increase of righteousness and the knowledge of the Lord, receive him as the Lord.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are instructed to receive teachers who uphold apostolic doctrine and advance righteousness while firmly rejecting those who teach contrary, corrupting doctrines.
passages.fullText: 1. Whosoever therefore shall come and teach you all these things that have been said before, receive him; 2. but if the teacher himself be perverted and teach a different doctrine to the destruction thereof, hear him not; 3. but if to the increase of righteousness and the knowledge of the Lord, receive him as the Lord.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 5. Let every apostle, when he cometh to you, be received as the Lord; 6. but he shall not abide more than a single day, or if there be need, a second likewise; 7. but if he abide three days, he is a false prophet. 8. And when he departeth let the apostle receive nothing save bread, until he findeth shelter; 9. but if he ask money, he is a false prophet.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Itinerant apostles are to be received as Christ Himself, yet must be tested for authenticity by their detachment from money and reluctance to burden the local church.
passages.fullText: 4. But concerning the apostles and prophets, so do ye according to the ordinance of the Gospel. 5. Let every apostle, when he cometh to you, be received as the Lord; 6. but he shall not abide more than a single day, or if there be need, a second likewise; 7. but if he abide three days, he is a false prophet. 8. And when he departeth let the apostle receive nothing save bread, until he findeth shelter; 9. but if he ask money, he is a false prophet.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 12. Yet not every one that speaketh in the Spirit is a prophet, but only if he have the ways of the Lord. 13. From his ways therefore the false prophet and the prophet shall be recognized.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: True charismatic prophecy is distinguished from false claims not merely by ecstatic speech, but by whether the speaker reflects the holy life and ways of Christ.
passages.fullText: 10. And any prophet speaking in the Spirit ye shall not try neither discern; 11. for every sin shall be forgiven, but this sin shall not be forgiven. 12. Yet not every one that speaketh in the Spirit is a prophet, but only if he have the ways of the Lord. 13. From his ways therefore the false prophet and the prophet shall be recognized.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 14. And no prophet when he ordereth a table in the Spirit shall eat of it; 15. otherwise he is a false prophet. 16. And every prophet teaching the truth, if he doeth not what he teacheth, is a false prophet.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A prophet is revealed as false if he uses spiritual authority for carnal self-indulgence or fails to practice the moral truths that he preaches.
passages.fullText: 14. And no prophet when he ordereth a table in the Spirit shall eat of it; 15. otherwise he is a false prophet. 16. And every prophet teaching the truth, if he doeth not what he teacheth, is a false prophet.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 17. And every prophet approved and found true, if he doeth ought as an outward mystery typical of the Church, and yet teacheth you not to do all that he himself doeth, shall not be judged before you; 18. he hath his judgment in the presence of God; 19. for in like manner also did the prophets of old time. 20. And whosoever shall say in the Spirit, Give me silver or anything else, ye shall not listen to him;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Approved prophets acting out symbolic mysteries are left to the judgment of God, but any prophet soliciting money in the Spirit must be rejected.
passages.fullText: 17. And every prophet approved and found true, if he doeth ought as an outward mystery typical of the Church, and yet teacheth you not to do all that he himself doeth, shall not be judged before you; 18. he hath his judgment in the presence of God; 19. for in like manner also did the prophets of old time. 20. And whosoever shall say in the Spirit, Give me silver or anything else, ye shall not listen to him;

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 21. but if he tell you to give on behalf of others that are in want, let no man judge him.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: A prophet or minister is not to be condemned when requesting contributions for the relief of those in need, as almsgiving for the poor reflects genuine charity.
passages.fullText: 21. but if he tell you to give on behalf of others that are in want, let no man judge him.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 1. But let every one that cometh in the name of the Lord be received; 2. and then when ye have tested him ye shall know him, for ye shall have understanding on the right hand and on the left.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are commanded to welcome and assist traveling Christians with fraternal hospitality while exercising prudent spiritual discernment.
passages.fullText: 1. But let every one that cometh in the name of the Lord be received; 2. and then when ye have tested him ye shall know him, for ye shall have understanding on the right hand and on the left. 3. If the comer is a traveller, assist him, so far as ye are able; 4. but he shall not stay with you more than two or three days, if it be necessary.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 5. But if he wishes to settle with you, being a craftsman, let him work for and eat his bread. 6. But if he has no craft, according to your wisdom provide how he shall live as a Christian among you, but not in idleness.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians intending to reside within a community are obligated to sustain themselves through honest labor, guarding against idleness and the exploitation of Christ's name.
passages.fullText: 5. But if he wishes to settle with you, being a craftsman, let him work for and eat his bread. 6. But if he has no craft, according to your wisdom provide how he shall live as a Christian among you, but not in idleness. 7. If he will not do this, he is trafficking upon Christ. 8. Beware of such men.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Every firstfruit then of the produce of the wine-vat and of the threshing-floor, of thy oxen and of thy sheep, thou shalt take and give as the firstfruit to the prophets; for they are your chief-priests.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christian ministers and teachers are worthy of sustenance, receiving the firstfruits of the community as chief priests or, in their absence, having those offerings given to the poor.
passages.fullText: 1. But every true prophet desiring to settle among you is worthy of his food. 2. In like manner a true teacher is also worthy, like the workman, of his food. 3. Every firstfruit then of the produce of the wine-vat and of the threshing-floor, of thy oxen and of thy sheep, thou shalt take and give as the firstfruit to the prophets; 4. for they are your chief-priests. 5. But if ye have not a prophet, give them to the poor.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: yea and of money and raiment and every possession take the firstfruit, as shall seem good to thee, and give according to the commandment.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Believers are commanded to dedicate the firstfruits of all their daily labor, goods, provisions, and possessions to the service of God's ministers.
passages.fullText: 6. If thou makest bread, take the firstfruit and give according to the commandment. 7. In like manner, when thou openest a jar of wine or of oil, take the firstfruit and give to the prophets; 8. yea and of money and raiment and every possession take the firstfruit, as shall seem good to thee, and give according to the commandment.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 1. And on the Lord's own day gather yourselves together and break bread and give thanks, first confessing your transgressions, that your sacrifice may be pure. 2. And let no man, having his dispute with his fellow, join your assembly until they have been reconciled, that your sacrifice may not be defiled;
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are commanded to gather on the Lord's Day to offer the pure Eucharistic sacrifice, preparing through confession of sins and fraternal reconciliation in fulfillment of prophetic Scripture.
passages.fullText: 1. And on the Lord's own day gather yourselves together and break bread and give thanks, first confessing your transgressions, that your sacrifice may be pure. 2. And let no man, having his dispute with his fellow, join your assembly until they have been reconciled, that your sacrifice may not be defiled; 3. for this sacrifice it is that was spoken of by the Lord: 4. In every place and at every time offer Me a pure sacrifice; 5. for I am a great king, saith the Lord and My name is wonderful among the nations.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Appoint for yourselves therefore bishops and deacons worthy of the Lord, men who are meek and not lovers of money, and true and approved; for unto you they also perform the service of the prophets and teachers.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are instructed to appoint worthy, virtuous bishops and deacons and to hold them in high esteem alongside prophets and teachers.
passages.fullText: 1. Appoint for yourselves therefore bishops and deacons worthy of the Lord, men who are meek and not lovers of money, and true and approved; 2. for unto you they also perform the service of the prophets and teachers. 3. Therefore despise them not; 4. for they are your honourable men along with the prophets and teachers.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And reprove one another, not in anger but in peace, as ye find in the Gospel; and let no one speak to any that has gone wrong towards his neighbour, neither let him hear a word from you, until he repent.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Fraternal correction must be carried out peacefully according to the Gospel, urging repentance before restoring fellowship to one who has wronged a neighbor.
passages.fullText: 5. And reprove one another, not in anger but in peace, as ye find in the Gospel; 6. and let no one speak to any that has gone wrong towards his neighbour, neither let him hear a word from you, until he repent.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But your prayers and your almsgivings and all your deeds so do ye as ye find it in the Gospel of our Lord.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: All prayers, works of charity, and daily actions of the faithful must be faithfully ordered according to the Gospel of Christ.
passages.fullText: 7. But your prayers and your almsgivings and all your deeds so do ye as ye find it in the Gospel of our Lord.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Be watchful for your life; let your lamps not be quenched and your loins not ungirded, but be ye ready; for ye know not the hour in which our Lord cometh.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are exhorted to constant spiritual vigilance, frequent assembly, and perseverance, since readiness at the final hour is essential for salvation.
passages.fullText: 1. Be watchful for your life; 2. let your lamps not be quenched and your loins not ungirded, but be ye ready; 3. for ye know not the hour in which our Lord cometh. 4. And ye shall gather yourselves together frequently, seeking what is fitting for your souls; 5. for the whole time of your faith shall not profit you, if ye be not perfected at the last season.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: For in the last days the false prophets and corrupters shall be multiplied, and the sheep shall be turned into wolves, and love shall be turned into hate. For as lawlessness increaseth, they shall hate one another and shall persecute and betray.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: In the end times, spiritual deception and lawlessness will escalate through false prophets, the breakdown of charity, and the arrival of the world-deceiver performing deceptive signs.
passages.fullText: 6. For in the last days the false prophets and corrupters shall be multiplied, and the sheep shall be turned into wolves, and love shall be turned into hate. 7. For as lawlessness increaseth, they shall hate one another and shall persecute and betray. 8. And then the world-deceiver shall appear as a son of God; 9. and shall work signs and wonders, and the earth shall be delivered into his hands; 10. and he shall do unholy things, which have never been since the world began.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Then all created mankind shall come to the fire of testing, and many shall be offended and perish; but they that endure in their faith shall be saved by the Curse Himself.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Mankind will undergo a severe trial of fiery testing, but those who persevere steadfastly in faith will attain salvation through Christ crucified.
passages.fullText: 11. Then all created mankind shall come to the fire of testing, and many shall be offended and perish; 12. but they that endure in their faith shall be saved by the Curse Himself.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And then shall the signs of the truth appear; first a sign of a rift in the heaven, then a sign of a voice of a trumpet, and thirdly a resurrection of the dead; yet not of all, but as it was said: The Lord shall come and all His saints with Him. Then shall the world see the Lord coming upon the clouds of heaven.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The climax of salvation history will be manifested by celestial signs, the trumpet blast, the resurrection of the saints, and the glorious return of the Lord upon the clouds.
passages.fullText: 13. And then shall the signs of the truth appear; 14. first a sign of a rift in the heaven, then a sign of a voice of a trumpet, and thirdly a resurrection of the dead; 15. yet not of all, but as it was said: 16. The Lord shall come and all His saints with Him. 17. Then shall the world see the Lord coming upon the clouds of heaven.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt do no murder, thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not corrupt boys, thou shalt not commit fornication, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not deal in magic, thou shalt do no sorcery, thou shalt not murder a child by abortion nor kill them when born, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's goods, thou shalt not perjure thyself, thou shalt not bear false witness, thou shalt not speak evil, thou shalt not cherish a grudge, thou shalt not be double-minded nor double-tongued; for the double tongue is a snare of death.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache sets forth the grave moral prohibitions of the Way of Life, strictly forbidding murder, sexual immorality, abortion, infanticide, sorcery, theft, and deceitful speech.
passages.fullText: 1. And this is the second commandment of the teaching. 2. Thou shalt do no murder, thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not corrupt boys, thou shalt not commit fornication, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not deal in magic, thou shalt do no sorcery, thou shalt not murder a child by abortion nor kill them when born, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's goods, thou shalt not perjure thyself, thou shalt not bear false witness, thou shalt not speak evil, thou shalt not cherish a grudge, thou shalt not be double-minded nor double-tongued; 3. for the double tongue is a snare of death.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not hate any man, but some thou shalt reprove, and for others thou shalt pray, and others thou shalt love more than thy life.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are commanded to maintain truthfulness in word and deed, renounce avarice and hypocrisy, and practice fraternal correction, intercession, and sacrificial love for neighbor.
passages.fullText: 4. Thy word shall not be false or empty, but fulfilled by action. 5. Thou shalt not be avaricious nor a plunderer nor a hypocrite nor ill-tempered nor proud. 6. Thou shalt not entertain an evil design against thy neighbour. 7. Thou shalt not hate any man, but some thou shalt reprove, and for others thou shalt pray, and others thou shalt love more than thy life.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: My child, flee from every evil and everything that resembleth it. Be not angry, for anger leadeth to murder, nor jealous nor contentious nor wrathful; for of all these things murders are engendered.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache instructs Christians to avoid not only grave sins like murder, but also the antecedent passions of wrath, jealousy, and contention.
passages.fullText: 1. My child, flee from every evil and everything that resembleth it. 2. Be not angry, for anger leadeth to murder, nor jealous nor contentious nor wrathful; 3. for of all these things murders are engendered.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: My child, be not lustful, for lust leadeth to fornication, neither foul-speaking neither with uplifted eyes; for of all these things adulteries are engendered.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Believers are exhorted to maintain custody of the eyes and speech to extinguish concupiscence before it leads to fornication and adultery.
passages.fullText: 4. My child, be not lustful, for lust leadeth to fornication, neither foul-speaking neither with uplifted eyes; 5. for of all these things adulteries are engendered.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: My child, be no dealer in omens, since it leads to idolatry, nor an enchanter nor an astrologer nor a magician, neither be willing to look at them; for from all these things idolatry is engendered.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache strictly forbids divination, astrology, and magical practices, warning that all occult engagement engenders idolatry.
passages.fullText: 6. My child, be no dealer in omens, since it leads to idolatry, nor an enchanter nor an astrologer nor a magician, neither be willing to look at them; 7. for from all these things idolatry is engendered.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: My child, be not a liar, since lying leads to theft, neither avaricious neither vainglorious; for from all these things thefts are engendered.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The author warns that dishonesty, avarice, and vainglory corrupt moral integrity and give birth to theft.
passages.fullText: 8. My child, be not a liar, since lying leads to theft, neither avaricious neither vainglorious; 9. for from all these things thefts are engendered.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: My child, be not a murmurer, since it leadeth to blasphemy, neither self-willed neither a thinker of evil thoughts; for from all these things blasphemies are engendered.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Murmuring, self-will, and malicious thoughts are condemned as spiritual vices that ultimately cultivate blasphemy against God.
passages.fullText: 10. My child, be not a murmurer, since it leadeth to blasphemy, neither self-willed neither a thinker of evil thoughts; 11. for from all these things blasphemies are engendered.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But be meek, since the meek shall inherit the earth. Be long-suffering and pitiful and guileless and quiet and kindly and always fearing the words which thou hast heard.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are called to embrace evangelical meekness, patience, simplicity of heart, and humble companionship with the righteous rather than the haughty.
passages.fullText: 12. But be meek, since the meek shall inherit the earth. 13. Be long-suffering and pitiful and guileless and quiet and kindly and always fearing the words which thou hast heard. 14. Thou shalt not exalt thyself, neither shalt thou admit boldness into thy soul. 15. Thy soul shall not cleave together with the lofty, but with the righteous and humble shalt thou walk.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: The accidents that befal thee thou shalt receive as good, knowing that nothing is done without God.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are taught to receive all happenings and trials as good, recognizing that all things are governed by God's all-encompassing providence.
passages.fullText: 16. The accidents that befal thee thou shalt receive as good, knowing that nothing is done without God.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: My child, thou shalt remember him that speaketh unto thee the word of God night and day, and shalt honour him as the Lord; for whencesoever the Lordship speaketh, there is the Lord.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are called to honor those who preach the word of God as the Lord Himself and to seek daily fellowship with the saints.
passages.fullText: 1. My child, thou shalt remember him that speaketh unto thee the word of God night and day, and shalt honour him as the Lord; 2. for whencesoever the Lordship speaketh, there is the Lord. 3. Moreover thou shalt seek out day by day the persons of the saints, that thou mayest find rest in their words.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not make a schism, but thou shalt pacify them that contend; thou shalt judge righteously, thou shalt not make a difference in a person to reprove him for transgressions.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Believers must foster peace, avoid division and schism, and execute righteous, impartial correction without human favoritism or hesitation.
passages.fullText: 4. Thou shalt not make a schism, but thou shalt pacify them that contend; 5. thou shalt judge righteously, thou shalt not make a difference in a person to reprove him for transgressions. 6. Thou shalt not doubt whether a thing shall be or not be.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: If thou hast ought passing through thy hands, thou shalt give a ransom for thy sins. Thou shalt not hesitate to give, neither shalt thou murmur when giving; for thou shalt know who is the good paymaster of thy reward.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Almsgiving serves as a spiritual remedy and ransom for sins, requiring a cheerful, ungrudging heart that trusts in God's divine recompense.
passages.fullText: 7. Be not thou found holding out thy hands to receive, but drawing them in as to giving. 8. If thou hast ought passing through thy hands, thou shalt give a ransom for thy sins. 9. Thou shalt not hesitate to give, neither shalt thou murmur when giving; 10. for thou shalt know who is the good paymaster of thy reward.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not turn away from him that is in want, but shalt make thy brother partaker in all things, and shalt not say that anything is thine own. For if ye are fellow-partakers in that which is imperishable, how much rather in the things which are perishable?
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Spiritual communion in heavenly goods obligates Christians to share earthly goods with those in need and to raise children diligently in the fear of God.
passages.fullText: 11. Thou shalt not turn away from him that is in want, but shalt make thy brother partaker in all things, and shalt not say that anything is thine own. 12. For if ye are fellow-partakers in that which is imperishable, how much rather in the things which are perishable? Thou shalt not withhold thy hand from thy son or from thy daughter, but from their youth thou shalt teach them the fear of God.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt not command thy bondservant or thine handmaid in thy bitterness, who trust in the same God as thyself, lest haply they should cease to fear the God who is over both of you; for He cometh, not to call men with respect of persons, but He cometh to those whom the Spirit hath prepared.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Masters and servants must fulfill their mutual duties with reverence, knowing that God judges impartially without regard to earthly status.
passages.fullText: 13. Thou shalt not command thy bondservant or thine handmaid in thy bitterness, who trust in the same God as thyself, lest haply they should cease to fear the God who is over both of you; 14. for He cometh, not to call men with respect of persons, but He cometh to those whom the Spirit hath prepared. 15. But ye, servants, shall be subject unto your masters, as to a type of God, in shame and fear.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Thou shalt never forsake the commandments of the Lord; but shalt keep those things which thou hast received, neither adding to them nor taking away from them.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful must reject hypocrisy and faithfully preserve the intact deposit of divine commandments without alteration.
passages.fullText: 16. Thou shalt hate all hypocrisy, and everything that is not pleasing to the Lord. 17. Thou shalt never forsake the commandments of the Lord; 18. but shalt keep those things which thou hast received, neither adding to them nor taking away from them.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: In church thou shalt confess thy transgressions, and shalt not betake thyself to prayer with an evil conscience. This is the way of life.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Way of Life requires the public confession of sins within the Church and approaching prayer with a purified conscience.
passages.fullText: 19. In church thou shalt confess thy transgressions, and shalt not betake thyself to prayer with an evil conscience. 20. This is the way of life.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: 1. But the way of death is this. 2. First of all, it is evil and full of a curse: murders, adulteries, lusts, fornications, thefts, idolatries, magical arts, witchcrafts, plunderings, false witnessings, hypocrisies, doubleness of heart, treachery, pride, malice, stubbornness, covetousness, foul-speaking, jealousy, boldness, exaltation, boastfulness; 3. persecutors of good men, hating truth, loving a lie, not perceiving the reward of righteousness, not cleaving to the good nor to righteous judgment, wakeful not for that which is good but for that which is evil; 4. from whom gentleness and forbearance stand aloof; 5. loving vain things, pursuing a recompense, not pitying the poor man, not toiling for him that is oppressed with toil, not recognizing Him that made them, murderers of children, corrupters of the creatures of God, turning away from him that is in want, oppressing him that is afflicted, advocates of the wealthy, unjust judges of the poor, altogether sinful. 6. May ye be delivered, my children, from all these things.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache catalogues the vices, injustices, and grave sins comprising the way of death—including idolatry, impurity, abortion, and oppression of the poor—urging the faithful to be delivered from all such evils.
passages.fullText: 1. But the way of death is this. 2. First of all, it is evil and full of a curse: murders, adulteries, lusts, fornications, thefts, idolatries, magical arts, witchcrafts, plunderings, false witnessings, hypocrisies, doubleness of heart, treachery, pride, malice, stubbornness, covetousness, foul-speaking, jealousy, boldness, exaltation, boastfulness; 3. persecutors of good men, hating truth, loving a lie, not perceiving the reward of righteousness, not cleaving to the good nor to righteous judgment, wakeful not for that which is good but for that which is evil; 4. from whom gentleness and forbearance stand aloof; 5. loving vain things, pursuing a recompense, not pitying the poor man, not toiling for him that is oppressed with toil, not recognizing Him that made them, murderers of children, corrupters of the creatures of God, turning away from him that is in want, oppressing him that is afflicted, advocates of the wealthy, unjust judges of the poor, altogether sinful. 6. May ye be delivered, my children, from all these things.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: See lest any man lead you astray from this way of righteousness, for he teacheth thee apart from God.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The faithful are warned to guard the true Apostolic way of righteousness against false teachers who instruct contrary to God.
passages.fullText: 1. See lest any man lead you astray from this way of righteousness, for he teacheth thee apart from God.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: For if thou art able to bear the whole yoke of the Lord, thou shalt be perfect; but if thou art not able, do that which thou art able.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: While bearing the full yoke of the Lord attains evangelical perfection, believers are counseled to faithfully perform all that they are capable of bearing.
passages.fullText: 2. For if thou art able to bear the whole yoke of the Lord, thou shalt be perfect; 3. but if thou art not able, do that which thou art able.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But concerning eating, bear that which thou art able; yet abstain by all means from meat sacrificed to idols; for it is the worship of dead gods.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are encouraged to practice dietary mortification according to their capacity, but are strictly commanded to abstain from food sacrificed to idols to avoid participating in false worship.
passages.fullText: 4. But concerning eating, bear that which thou art able; 5. yet abstain by all means from meat sacrificed to idols; 6. for it is the worship of dead gods.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Having first recited all these things, baptize in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit in living (running) water. But if thou hast neither, then pour water on the head thrice in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache prescribes the valid form and matter for Holy Baptism, commanding the invocation of the Most Holy Trinity and allowing for baptism by affusion when running or cold water is unavailable.
passages.fullText: 1. But concerning baptism, thus shall ye baptize. 2. Having first recited all these things, baptize in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit in living (running) water. 3. But if thou hast not living water, then baptize in other water; 4. and if thou art not able in cold, then in warm. 5. But if thou hast neither, then pour water on the head thrice in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But before the baptism let him that baptizeth and him that is baptized fast, and any others also who are able; and thou shalt order him that is baptized to fast a day or two before.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Sacramental initiation requires ascetical preparation, mandating that the minister, the catechumen, and able members of the community fast prior to the administration of Baptism.
passages.fullText: 6. But before the baptism let him that baptizeth and him that is baptized fast, and any others also who are able; 7. and thou shalt order him that is baptized to fast a day or two before.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: And let not your fastings be with the hypocrites, for they fast on the second and the fifth day of the week; but do ye keep your fast on the fourth and on the preparation (the sixth) day.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Christians are instructed to practice ascetical fasting distinctly on Wednesdays and Fridays rather than following the fasting schedule of the hypocrites.
passages.fullText: 1. And let not your fastings be with the hypocrites, for they fast on the second and the fifth day of the week; 2. but do ye keep your fast on the fourth and on the preparation (the sixth) day.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: Neither pray ye as the hypocrites, but as the Lord commanded in His Gospel, thus pray ye: Our Father, which art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name; Thy kingdom come; Thy will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth; give us this day our daily bread; and forgive us our debt, as we also forgive our debtors; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one; for Thine is the power and the glory for ever and ever. Three times in the day pray ye so.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache transmits the Lord's Prayer as commanded in the Gospel, instructing the faithful to recite this vocal prayer three times daily.
passages.fullText: 3. Neither pray ye as the hypocrites, but as the Lord commanded in His Gospel, thus pray ye: 4. Our Father, which art in heaven, hallowed be Thy name; 5. Thy kingdom come; 6. Thy will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth; 7. give us this day our daily bread; 8. and forgive us our debt, as we also forgive our debtors; 9. and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one; 10. for Thine is the power and the glory for ever and ever. 11. Three times in the day pray ye so.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: We give Thee thanks, O our Father, for the holy vine of Thy son David, which Thou madest known unto us through Thy Son Jesus; Thine is the glory for ever and ever.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The Didache sets forth the liturgical thanksgiving over the Eucharistic cup, praising God the Father for the holy vine of David revealed through Jesus Christ.
passages.fullText: 1. But as touching the eucharistic thanksgiving give ye thanks thus. 2. First, as regards the cup: 3. We give Thee thanks, O our Father, for the holy vine of Thy son David, which Thou madest known unto us through Thy Son Jesus; 4. Thine is the glory for ever and ever.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: As this broken bread was scattered upon the mountains and being gathered together became one, so may Thy Church be gathered together from the ends of the earth into Thy kingdom; for Thine is the glory and the power through Jesus Christ for ever and ever.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: The liturgical blessing over the broken bread gives thanks for life and knowledge in Christ, praying that the Church scattered across the earth may be gathered into one in God's kingdom.
passages.fullText: 5. Then as regards the broken bread: 6. We give Thee thanks, O our Father, for the life and knowledge which Thou didst make known unto us through Thy Son Jesus; 7. Thine is the glory for ever and ever. 8. As this broken bread was scattered upon the mountains and being gathered together became one, so may Thy Church be gathered together from the ends of the earth into Thy kingdom; 9. for Thine is the glory and the power through Jesus Christ for ever and ever.

passages.author: The Apostolic Fathers (Trans. J. B. Lightfoot)
passages.keyExcerpt: But let no one eat or drink of this eucharistic thanksgiving, but they that have been baptized into the name of the Lord; for concerning this also the Lord hath said: Give not that which is holy to the dogs.
passages.oneSentenceSummary: Participation in the Holy Eucharist is strictly reserved for those who have received Christian Baptism, guarding the sacred mysteries from profanation.
passages.fullText: 10. But let no one eat or drink of this eucharistic thanksgiving, but they that have been baptized into the name of the Lord; 11. for concerning this also the Lord hath said: 12. Give not that which is holy to the dogs.
